label: Ubiquiti UF-Nano G GPON ONT, 1x GE
notes: The box is the datasheet's: one SC/APC GPON WAN port at 2.488 Gbit/s down and 1.244 Gbit/s up, one Gigabit LAN, 24 V passive PoE, up to 128 per OLT GPON port. The optical window is not the datasheet's, deliberately. Ubiquiti prints the UF-Nano G as TX (Class B+) 1.5 to 5 dBm, RX -8 to -28 dBm, and those are the OLT-side class B+ figures reprinted for the ONU: ITU-T G.984.2 Table III.1 puts an ONU at +0.5..+5 dBm launch with -27 dBm sensitivity and -8 dBm overload. This row carries the standard's ONU window and not the printed pair, because the upstream budget is set by the weakest ONU on a shared ODN: a plan leaning on a +1 dBm floor and a -28 dBm receiver is 1 dB optimistic in each direction the day a different ONT joins the same PON, and a printed pair that matches the OLT column is more likely a reprint than a measurement. If every ONT on the plant is a UF-Nano G and the sheet is right, both directions gain about 1 dB - that is a decision to write down in the plan, not a default. Only the class is asserted here: replace the row with the ONT actually installed, because the budget moves with its measured sensitivity.
